title: FA/69/2011 of RAJESH SINGH NEGI Vs R.C.NIRULA AND SONS HUF

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
First Appeal No. 69 of 2011
Rajesh Singh Negi .....Ö.ÖÖ Appellant
versus
R.C.Nirula & Sons (HUF) ÖÖÖÖ. Respondent
Mr. Sarvesh Agarwal, Advocate, present for the appellant.
None appears for the respondent.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
1. A suit for declaration, prohibitory and mandatory
injection was filed by the plaintiff/appellant in the
Court of Civil Judge, Senior Division, Nainital. The
same was dismissed vide impugned judgment and
order dated 20.05.2011. Aggrieved against the
same, present First Appeal was preferred by the
plaintiff-appellant. The plaintiff relied upon
agreement to sell dated 18.06.2009 (annexure-3)
executed by the defendant (respondent herein) in
his favour. The plaintiff also relied upon a receipt
of the selfsame date, whereby the defendant
received a sum of Rs. 10 lacs from the plaintiff in
respect of the property in question. Reliance was
also placed upon disclaimer deed of the selfsame

2
date, executed by the defendant in favour of the
plaintiff in respect of the disputed property. The
most-important piece of paper is possession letter
dated 18.06.2009 signed by the defendant in
favour of the plaintiff. It will be worthwhile to
reproduce herein the contents of the said
possession letter:
ì I, Mr. R.C.Nirula, karta on behalf of R.C.Nirula
and Sons HUF, s/o late Mr. P.R. Nirula, r/o 52 Golf
Link, New Delhi-110003 has today handed over the
physical vacant and peaceful possession of the
bearing Cottage No. A-8, at the Corbett, Brinshop
Road, Sukhatal, Nainital, Uttarakhand measuring
1300 sq. fts. Therein of the said cottage with
exclusive roof right to Mr. Rajesh Singh Negi, s/o
Mr. Shankar Singh Negi, r/o B-53, Paryavaran
Complex, IGNOU Road, New Delhi-110030, and
have put in possession today on the day of executing
and signing of the present possession letter and that
they have come in possession of the same as absolute
owner therein.î
2. Defendant (respondent herein) admitted all the
plaint averments in his written statement. It will be
appropriate to reproduce paras 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 7 and
9 of the written statement herein below:-
ìi. That the contents of para no. 1 and 2 of the plaint
are admitted.
ii. That the contents of para no. 3 7 4 of the plaint are
admitted. The defendant has received the entire
amount of sale consideration as stated by the plaintiff
in the paras under reply.
iii. That in reply to the contents of para nos. 5, 6 & 7 of
the plaint, it is submitted that the defendant executed
an agreement of sale with regard to the property in
question on 18.06.2009 in favour of the plaintiff and in
pursuance of the said agreement, the defendant handed
over the vacant actual and physical possession of the
suit property to the plaintiff and has also executed a

3
possession letter in favour of the plaintiff. Moreover,
the defendant also executed a disclaimer deed in
respect of suit property in favour of the plaintiff. The
defendant has also handed over the documents
pertaining to original chain of title in respect of suit
property to the plaintiff.
iv. That in reply to the contents of para no. 8,9,10 and
11 of the plaint, it is submitted that since the defendant
is of old age and is not able to come to Nainital
personally to execute the sale-deed in favour of the
plaintiff in respect of the suit property as such the sale-deed could not be executed in favour of the plaintiff. It
is further submitted that the defendant appointed one
Sri Satish Chandra Jha as his power of attorney holder
on his behalf to execute the said sale-deed in favour of
the plaintiff but the same could not be executed.
v. That the contents of para no.12 of the plaint are
admitted. The defendant acknowledges that the
plaintiff has made full and final payment of the sale
consideration to the defendant and as such the plaintiff
has a legitimate right, title and interest in property in
suit and is in actual physical possession thereof.
vii. That the contents of para no. 15 of the plaint are
admitted.
ix. That in reply to the contents of para no. 18 of the
plaint it is submitted that the answering defendant has
no objection if the plaintiff be declared as the sole
owner and in possession of the property in suit."
3. The Trial Court framed three issues, which are
enumerated herein below for reference:
(i) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to be
declared as owner of cottage no. A-8,
situated at ëthe Corbettí Brinshop Road,
Sukhatal, Mallital, Nainital? If so, itís
effect?

4
(ii) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to reliefs
ëBí and ëCí as claimed by him in respect
of the suit property? If so, itís effect?
(iii) To what relief, if any, is the plaintiff
entitled?
4. The Trial Court deliberated upon the documents
filed on behalf of the plaintiff to hold that since
they were not the registered documents, therefore,
no cognizance of the same could be taken. In other
words, the trial court held that since the
documents, on the basis of which, the plaintiffís-claim is based, are not the registered documents,
therefore, no right flows to the plaintiff on the basis
of such unregistered documents. There appears to
be no infirmity in the said findings of the trial
court in so far as the evidentiary value of the
unregistered document is concerned.
5. But learned trial court committed a mistake in not
framing an important issue. ëPossessioní is sine
qua non of any suit for claiming the relief of
permanent prohibitory injunction. No issue in that
respect was framed by the trial court. Framing of
that issue was also necessary in view of the
ëpossession-letterí given by the defendant to the
plaintiff. The defendant has admitted handing over
the possession of the disputed property to the
plaintiff-appellant in his written statement. Issue
of ëpossessioní was neither framed nor discussed
while delivering the impugned judgment and order.

5
6. It may be noted here that the defendant
(respondent herein) was served through
publication in the ëTimes of Indiaí, Delhi edition
dated 27th December, 2013, but none has
responded for the respondent despite such
substituted service.
7. Order XII Rule 6 C.P.C. provides as follows:
"6. Judgment on admissions.- (1) Where admissions of
fact have been made either in the pleading or otherwise,
whether orally or in writing, the court may at any stage of
the suit, either on the application of an party or of its own
motion and without waiting for the determination of any
other question between the parties, make such Order or
give such judgment as It may think fit, having regard to
such admissions.
(2) Whenever a judgment is pronounced under sub-rule (1)
a decree shall be drawn up in accordance with the
judgment and the decree shall bear the date on which the
judgment was pronounced."
8. Further, Sub-Rule (3) of Rule 1 of Order 14
provides that each material proposition affirmed by
one party and denied by the other, shall form the
subject of a distinct issue.
9. In the instant case, although all the plaint
averments were accepted and admitted by the
defendant in his written statement, but the
problem arose because the documents as regards
ownership filed on behalf of the plaintiff, were
unregistered documents. No issue was framed as
regards ëpossessioní, although ëpossession-letterí
was filed on behalf of the plaintiff and admitted by
the defendant. Such ëpossession-letterí did not

6
require compulsory registration. It, therefore,
becomes imperative for this Court to remit the
matter back to the trial court for framing an issue
in respect of ëpossessioní and then, decide the
matter according to law, after affording due
opportunity of hearing to the parties.
10. Learned trial court is, therefore, directed to frame
an additional issue as follows:
"4. Whether the plaintiff is in possession of the disputed
cottage as claimed by him in para 6 of the plaint? If so, its
effect?î
11. First appeal is accordingly allowed. Impugned
Judgment and decree dated 20.05.2011, passed by
Civil Judge (S.D.), Nainital is set aside. The matter
is remitted back to the court below for framing an
additional issue and then decide the same after
affording due opportunity of hearing to the parties
concerned according to law.
12. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the court
below for compliance.
13. It is provided that no third party interest shall be
created by the defendant (respondent herein) over
the suit property, till decision of the Original Suit
No. 84 of 2009.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.)
 23.06.2014
Kaushal
